purpose: Match 1 concern that the agent wrote to a route table row, or confirm that no row covers it.

options.project-setup: xcconfig|build setting|build configuration|code signing|provisioning profile|swiftlint|swift-format|lint rule|package\.resolved|new dependency|third-party (package|library|sdk)
options.architecture: feature registry|dependency injection|composition root|domain target|feature package|local package
options.lifecycle-extensions: widget|live activit|app intent|siri|push notification|background task|scene phase|share extension|app extension
options.testing: unit test|ui test|snapshot test|test coverage|swift testing|xctest|test plan
options.release: testflight|app store submission|app store connect|phased release|version number|build number|app review

state_fields.concern: 1 concern of the change, in the words of the agent.

row.instructions: Which topic of the iOS architecture guide covers the concern in `concern`? Pick the closest topic.

criteria.project-setup: A new project, build settings, .xcconfig files, signing, a new dependency, or linting.
criteria.architecture: A feature, a package, domain or model code, dependency injection, or the feature registry.
criteria.ui-framework: SwiftUI or UIKit views, web content, custom drawing, or the design system.
criteria.navigation: Routes, navigation stacks, deep links, or universal links.
criteria.networking: HTTP calls, WebSockets, GraphQL, streams, or offline display.
criteria.persistence: Stored data, schemas, migrations of stored data, caches, or App Group data.
criteria.security-privacy: Secrets, input across a trust boundary, logs, permissions, personal or regulated data, or AI features.
criteria.concurrency: Async code, actors, Sendable, error handling, randomness, clocks, sync, or crash reports.
criteria.lifecycle-extensions: Scene phases, background tasks, push notifications, extensions, widgets, or App Intents.
criteria.accessibility: Use of a view or a control with assistive technologies.
criteria.localization: Text the user sees, dates, numbers, currency, or measurements.
criteria.testing: Tests, test tools, coverage, or test automation.
criteria.performance: Launch time, scrolling, images, memory, or performance budgets.
criteria.purchases-seams: Purchases, entitlements, analytics, or feature flags.
criteria.release: Versions, release builds, TestFlight, or App Store submission.
criteria.migration: An existing app, legacy code, CocoaPods, Swift 5, UIKit screens, or a port from another technology.
criteria.deviations: A change to a default, or a choice between patterns or stores.
criteria.native-ui-patterns: Screen layout, platform UI conventions, or flow design.

row_applies.instructions: Does a topic of the iOS architecture guide cover the concern in `concern`?

criteria.true: The concern is about 1 of these topics: project setup, build settings, signing, dependencies, or linting; features, packages, domain code, or dependency injection; SwiftUI or UIKit views, web content, custom drawing, or the design system; navigation, deep links, or universal links; HTTP calls, WebSockets, GraphQL, or offline display; sign-in, tokens, accounts, or biometrics; stored data, schemas, caches, or App Group data; secrets, input across a trust boundary, logs, permissions, personal or regulated data, or AI features; async code, actors, error handling, clocks, sync, or crash reports; scene phases, background tasks, push notifications, extensions, widgets, or App Intents; accessibility; localized text, dates, numbers, currency, or measurements; tests; launch time, scrolling, images, memory, or performance budgets; purchases, entitlements, analytics, or feature flags; versions, TestFlight, or App Store submission; an existing app, legacy code, or a port from another technology; a change to a default pattern or store; screen layout or platform UI conventions.
criteria.false: No topic above covers the concern.

actions.<row>: Read references/<row>.md. For native-ui-patterns, load the native-ui-patterns skill.
actions.none: The concern is out of bounds. Research it in primary sources and write a decision record.
